title: Purely inseparable integral extensions have a unique prime over each prime
statement: Let $A\subseteq B$ be an extension of integral domains with $B$ finitely generated as an $A$-module, assume that $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let the fraction fields $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)\subseteq L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ (the inclusion induced by $A\subseteq B$) form a finite purely inseparable extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ there is exactly one prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, that is, with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, proof, sentence 'Since A subset B subset C are finite and L/M/K are purely inseparable ... there is a unique prime lying over p'; the integral/radicial argument is made explicit

proof.text: (Some power of every element of $B$ lies in $A$.) Let $e$ be the characteristic exponent of $K$: $e=1$ if $\operatorname{char}K=0$ and $e=p$ if $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$; $L$ has the same characteristic as $K$. We show: for every $b\in B$ there is $n\ge0$ with $b^{e^n}\in A$. Regard $b\in B\subseteq L$. Since $L/K$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], there is $n\ge0$ with $c:=b^{e^n}\in K$ (in characteristic $p$ this is the definition; in characteristic $0$ the definition gives $L=K$, and $n=0$). Now $c\in B$, and $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, so $c$ is integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]: $c^m+a_{m-1}c^{m-1}+\dots+a_0=0$ in $B$ with $a_i\in A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. This equation holds in $L$, all its terms lie in the subfield $K$ (as $c\in K$, $a_i\in A\subseteq K$), and $K\to L$ is injective, so it holds in $K$: $c\in K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A$. As $A$ is a normal domain, integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $c\in A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring, line 12306), proof: 'Since A ⊂ B ⊂ C are finite and L/M/K are purely inseparable we see that for every element of B or C some power of it lies in A'; the use of normality is written out by the worker

proof.text: (Existence.) The inclusion $\varphi:A\to B$ is injective, and $B$ is integral over $A$ because it is a finitely generated $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. By lying over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] there is a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BR8 (lemma-powers, line 10718), proof, first paragraph (injectivity) and the surjectivity via Lemma Tag 00GQ

proof.text: (Uniqueness.) Let $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q'\subset B$ be primes with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q'\cap A$. Let $x\in\mathfrak q$. By Step 1 there is $n\ge0$ with $x^{e^n}\in A$; since $\mathfrak q$ is an ideal, $x^{e^n}\in\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q'$, and since $\mathfrak q'$ is prime and $e^n\ge1$, $x\in\mathfrak q'$. Hence $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q'$, and exchanging the roles of $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q'$ gives $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$; so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q'$. With Step 2, exactly one prime of $B$ lies over $\mathfrak p$.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07PR (proof sentence) and made precise, meaning unchanged: 'finite integral extension' is now 'B finitely generated as an A-module' (what the citer lem-weil-pbc-helper-g-ring-char-p provides and integrality follows from), the inclusion K ⊆ L is said to be induced by A ⊆ B, and 'lying over' is written as q ∩ A = p. Proof in 3 steps: (1) every b in B has b^{e^n} in A (e the characteristic exponent), from pure inseparability, integrality of a finite algebra (existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral) and normality of A; 07PR asserts this without mentioning normality, which is where it is needed (A regular there); (2) existence by lying over, new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over (Stacks 00GQ, RingHom.IsIntegral.comap_surjective, Topology.lean:1226); (3) uniqueness elementary from step 1 as in the proof of Stacks 0BR8: q ⊆ q' and symmetrically, so incomparability (lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability) is not needed.
